name: Private credit stress
value: Q3 BDC tenders above 5% caps; 15 of 55 prorated
summary: Non-traded BDC tender requests still exceed 5% caps; 15 of 55 prorated in Q3; no forced sales or bank losses found
state: Q3 tender requests at non-traded BDCs ran well above 5% quarterly offers: 16.8% at Blue Owl Credit Income, down from 21.9% in Q1 (SEC filing, 2 Oct), and about 10% at BCRED, with 15 of 55 BDCs prorating (Crowdfunded Wealth tracker, updated 7 Nov). Blue Owl reports $11.2bn of liquidity and says it can meet tenders without disposing of private loans. Limits at large funds have persisted across quarters and are read here as continuing rather than a new wave of gating. Searches on 8 Nov found no forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Holders of non-traded BDC shares may receive only part of a requested redemption and can wait several quarters for the rest. Bank and insurer lending to these funds is the route by which stress would spread more widely.
rubric_hit: Large funds limit redemptions at 5% caps (Watch); no forced asset sales or bank or insurer losses found for Alert

sources.title: SEC — Blue Owl Credit Income Corp. Form 8-K shareholder update
Crowdfunded Wealth — BDC Tender Offer Results, Q3 2026: Who Prorated, Who Paid

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
